rows.synopsis: Jane, David, and Greybeard track a polar bear in the Arctic Circle, inspiring Jane to convince her neighbor Mr. Jin to see trash differently.
rows.situation: wanting to help a wild animal and learning to understand her before rushing in
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Ursus Maritimus' title card): avalanche, snowmobile chase, tag-the-polar-bear mission. Learns: understanding comes before helping, and being scared as an explorer means you want to come home safely (explorer Jill Heinerth). Coping note: fear reframed as a safety signal. Content considerations: an avalanche, polar bears forced to eat garbage, vanishing sea ice. Secondary mirrors: a voicemail to Dad that goes unanswered, and learning to share (the promised snowmobile ride). Topic note: wild-creature drama mapped under the Batch 3 Prehistoric Planet judgment, same lens as all Jane rows.

rows.synopsis: While trying to tag a great white shark, Jane urges David's dad and Tata to rethink how they shop for groceries.
rows.situation: being scared of an animal and replacing that fear with respect
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Carcharodon carcharias' title card): cage dive, seal decoy, paella grocery run. Learns: sharks bite by mistake, almost never on purpose, and respect beats fear (marine biologist Carlee Jackson). Coping note: her reframe, replace the fear of sharks with respect for sharks. Content considerations: shark-attack talk throughout, nothing on screen. Secondary mirror: Tata's paella shopping list changes after the sustainable-seafood lesson.

rows.synopsis: David shrinks Jane and Greybeard to honeybee size to explore a hive. But when a schoolmate threatens the bees, Jane swoops in.
rows.situation: watching someone hurt a small creature and finding your voice to stop it
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Apis mellifera' title card): shrink-ship hive visit, Kurtis throws rocks at the hive, Jadiel stung. Learns: bees sting only to protect their home, and telling the truth about a creature turns an enemy into a planter of seedballs. Content considerations: rocks thrown at a beehive, a child stung, bees vanishing worldwide.

rows.synopsis: The trio take off on a mission to aid the flying fox when Greybeard accidentally parachutes into a neighbor's yard.
rows.situation: losing a beloved toy and discovering the neighbor everyone fears
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Acerodon jubatus' title card): parachute drop, Greybeard blown into the feared neighbor's garden. Learns: a feared neighbor can turn out to be kind, and when you start to understand a creature you start to care (flying-fox expert Lisa Paguntalan). Content considerations: a lost toy who is scared, a mom's no-shouting-on-work-calls rule broken, vampire-bat myths corrected, an endangered species (10,000 to 20,000 left).

rows.synopsis: Jane, David, and Greybeard try to sniff out why the gharial has a bulbed snout. A day at the pool points Jane toward an answer.
rows.situation: chores first, mission after: what a community asks back
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Gavialis gangeticus' title card): boat capers, co-op chores, new kid Andre. Learns: a co-op runs on everyone doing their part, and the unloved weird-looking animal deserves help too ('it's not only the cute and cuddly animals that matter', herpetologist Dr. Ruchira Somaweera). Content considerations: only about 600 gharials left, Greybeard falls in the pool. Secondary mirror: David's weekend with Dad and Sasha comes up lightly.

rows.synopsis: The three friends travel deep into the ocean to figure out why the blue whale sings, and Jane confronts a litterbug with a gifted voice.
rows.situation: a science mission that turns into a rescue
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Balaenoptera musculus' title card): a fishing net caught in the blue whale's mouth. Learns: change happens by listening, then starting a dialogue (Jane owns her own yelling: 'I shouldn't have yelled before'), and asking a shy neighbor to use her voice saves a whale. Coping note: the rescue lands through song and 'we're all in this together'. Content considerations: a whale could starve from the net, ocean plastic and ship strikes explained (whale scientist Asha de Vos). Secondary mirror: Mom's singing, and laundry that must be finished first.

rows.synopsis: A bug-sized Jane and Greybeard follow a monarch butterfly's journey to Mexico, leading Jane to seek assistance from Mr. Patel's green thumb.
rows.situation: a small problem nobody takes seriously
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Danaus plexippus' title card): Millie's lost key chain brushed off by David, Mr. Patel's milkweed refusal. Learns: small problems matter and small help adds up ('whether it's really small or really large, it all adds up', monarch scientist Patrick); David learns to take his sister seriously. Content considerations: monarchs declining every year, a grumpy neighbor who turns around. Secondary mirror: young conservationists Genevieve, Aiden and Joel shown helping.

rows.synopsis: Jane, David, and Greybeard monitor a black rhino and a red-billed oxpecker, whose relationship teaches them the value of teamwork.
rows.situation: two partners who work differently learning they are stronger together
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Diceros bicornis' title card): a rhino charge ('rhin-overed'), the oxpecker mirror, the big argument ('stop being scared all the time' vs 'stop telling me what to do'). Learns: like rhino and oxpecker, the pair watches each other's backs (rhino vet Dr. Matthew Mutinda on symbiosis). Content considerations: poaching explained, a rhino charges and nearly tramples them, habitat loss and climate change named. Secondary mirror: they start a conservation club at school (the Kitui Club).

rows.synopsis: Chasing a herd of caribou stirs up David's appetite. At lunch, David's grandpa tells a story about respect, responsibility, and sharing.
rows.situation: hunger and impatience on a mission that will not hurry
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Rangifer tarandus' title card): cold hiding, a spooked calf, Grandpa James's lunch story. Learns: take only what you need and share what you learn (Grandpa's story keeps knowledge alive; Caribou Guardian Starr Gauthier on elders stopping the hunt). Coping note: the lunch break and Grandpa's story settle David's hunger and hurry. Content considerations: a herd nearly tramples the crew (played for wonder), food waste and a landfill visit suggested. Topics note: the food and waste thread is a subplot, so no second topic tag.

rows.synopsis: Jane and David stay up past their bedtime to track a tiger that prefers to come out at night, and they stumble upon something in the garden shed.
rows.situation: bedtime trouble: one more mission after lights-out
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Panthera tigris' title card): night-vision tracking, a friend's jump-scare prank, Mom's shrinking time windows (ten minutes, five, three). Learns: even the fiercest animal needs space and quiet, and helping fits inside the time you are given (forest patroller Nayla Azmi). Content considerations: darkness and stalking talk ('it'll sneak up behind you'), fewer than 4,000 wild tigers, a bedtime boundary held warmly.

rows.synopsis: Jane, David, and Greybeard must reunite a lost baby panda with its mother—and find out why they're the only bears with six fingers.
rows.situation: a lost baby needs its mother, and nobody may touch
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Ailuropoda melanoleuca' title card): a baby panda (Rollie) separated from his mother, zip-line rescue. Learns: wild babies stay wild (observe, never pet), and nerves shrink when you name them (Mom before her date: 'I don't know why I'm feeling so nervous' / 'Because you like him'). Content considerations: baby-panda predators named (snow leopard, jackal, marten), pandas downgraded from endangered to vulnerable, panda-costume pee-spray gag. Secondary mirror: David's dads babysit during Mom's date.

rows.synopsis: Tracking a wolf in the snowy mountains leads the trio to their neighbor's pug, who helps connect the dots between wolves, dogs, and people.
rows.situation: watching someone leave the pack, and calling them back from far away
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Canis lupus' title card): a lone she-wolf's howl, moving day for Mr. Abbasi (off to college), Pugsley the runaway pug. Learns: wolves howl to tell each other where they are, and the lone wolf finds her pack ('they look so happy they found each other'); a person leaving can be talked through. Content considerations: moving day and a dog missing his person, wolf-attack fear corrected ('wolves rarely attack people'). Secondary mirror: the kids' new dog-walking business and its naming compromise.

rows.synopsis: The three friends use their underground vessel to observe the elusive pink fairy armadillo, but a garden problem stops them in their tracks.
rows.situation: chasing the animal nobody has ever studied
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Chlamyphorus truncatus' title card): a car nearly hits the armadillo, falling rocks nearly crush the crew, the garden mishap with Annisa. Learns: even the tiniest and oddest animal deserves study (armadillo expert Mariella Superina), and wild ones stay wild ('keep them in your heart and leave them in the wild'). Coping note: the crew retreats, rethinks the plan and returns. Content considerations: near-miss traffic and rockfall, pet trade and climate change named as threats. Topic note: no controlled topic fits a tiny-burrower conservation story; the digging machine is the mission's vehicle, not the subject.

rows.synopsis: While exploring the Great Barrier Reef to determine if coral is a plant or an animal, the trio learn that looks can be deceiving.
rows.situation: acting on what you believe, then owning it when you got it wrong
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Anthozoa' title card): Jane frees an illegal fisherman's catch, Mom makes it right ('Apologize or we're going home'). Learns: things are not always as simple as they seem; the fisherman turns out to be a citizen scientist and the parrotfish was helping, not hurting. Content considerations: fish taken from a person (returned), coral bleaching and overfishing, a lobster-trap scar story. Secondary mirror: the co-op vegetable garden and food eco-footprint close the episode. Topic note: Food & cooking tagged on that closing action, Monsters & magic on the reef story.

rows.synopsis: With David sick in bed, Jane must partner with an unexpected ally to save Greybeard from a pride of lions.
rows.situation: needing a busy parent right now
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Panthera leo' title card): David home sick, Mom on a mortgage call, Jane interrupting ('Mom. Mom, please.'). Learns: everyone has a job in a pride, and a mom on a work call is not a less loving mom; sick David learns rest is his job (lion expert Thandiwe Mweetwa). Coping note: Jane waits out the call, and Mom shows up when it is a real animal mission. Content considerations: a sick child, a lioness stalks the toy, about 23,000 lions left. Secondary mirror: the bake-sale-or-lemonade fundraiser plan.

rows.synopsis: Jane, David, and Greybeard set off to find out why hippos give birth away from their pods, while trying to reunite a baby hippo with her mom.
rows.situation: chores now, mission after, and a crying baby who needs holding
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Hippopotamus amphibius' title card): a hippo charges the boat, couch-cushion chores, neighbor Jillian's baby Ren who cries unless held. Learns: small jobs protect big things (fixing the couch, recycling batteries so more habitat is not dug up), and a fussy baby settles with a calm, willing holder (David with Ren). Content considerations: a hippo tops the boat, a crying baby, battery chemicals explained. Secondary mirror: the lobby sculpture made of recycled plastic (safari guide Kabelo Kgafela).

rows.synopsis: The trio head underground to dig into wombat defense tactics. Jane wants the community BBQ menu to explore new options.
rows.situation: loving something wild and letting it go
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Lasiorhinus krefftii' title card): burrow chase, the square-poo discovery, young expert Joey's orphan-wombat story. Learns: a goodbye can be the kindest thing you give (Joey's rescued joey was meant to be 'the ecosystem engineer he was always meant to be'), and people caring for country is part of the answer. Coping note: the goodbye reframed as what the wombat was meant to be. Content considerations: a mother wombat killed on a road (told in the rescue story), predators, wildfires, habitat loss. Secondary mirror: Jane's community BBQ menu push.

rows.synopsis: David joins Jane on a high-flying mission to chart an albatross' journey instead of helping his sister Millie.
rows.situation: your sibling's big moment versus your own mission
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Diomedea exulans' title card): Millie's unicorn-vs-fairy birthday planning set against the albatross charting mission. Learns: helping a sibling's party does not cost you your mission (David joins, reuses unicorn decorations), and the albatross's dance teaches that partners take turns (seabird scientist Sarah). Content considerations: near-crashes in flight, birds drowned by longline fishing hooks (the Hookpod fix), ocean plastic. Topic note: Birthday & party tagged on Millie's genuine throughline, Monsters & magic on the creature story.

rows.synopsis: Jane convinces her reluctant abuela to help get a baby elephant back to his family, where she uncovers why herds follow a matriarch.
rows.situation: a grandparent minding you who would rather relax
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Loxodonta africana' title card): Abuela's reluctant yes (with a promise to tidy up), the baby elephant lured to safety with a walkie-talkie, David's loud singing masking the cries. Learns: herds follow the oldest girl, and grandmothers turn out to be matriarchs too; Jane learns to bring Abuela along at her pace. Content considerations: a lioness closes in on the baby (resolved safely), poaching and habitat loss explained (Walona Sehularo of Elephants for Africa). Secondary mirror: breakfast led by the household's own matriarch.

rows.synopsis: Jane and Greybeard lose hope when they see how humans impact chimpanzees in the wild, but David and a special friend restore her faith.
rows.situation: seeing how much harm people cause, and holding onto hope anyway
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: opens on the 'Pan troglodytes' title card): the cleared forest, Mr. Jin the neighbor, the Chimp Eden sanctuary call. Learns: hope is something survivors teach you ('they become healthy, and they don't give up. And that is giving me hope', caregiver Stany, named by Jane Goodall), and your one part joins everyone else's. Coping note: Mom notices the drop and sets up the sanctuary call that restores hope. Content considerations: the heaviest content this season, handled gently: deforestation, hunting, chimpanzees taken as pets and circus performers, sick rescued chimps. Secondary mirror: the clean-your-room-then-save-the-world rule.

rows.synopsis: Charles and Lizzie meet Goldie, a golden retriever pup who teaches them an important life lesson.
rows.situation: sibling rivalry over a puppy, and doing what is best for the dog
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: the rescued golden pup is Goldie): a fire rescue, the blanket fort for a storm-scared puppy. Learns: love means doing what is best for the dog, not winning her ('the most important thing about being a good parent is doing what's best for your kids'... and Goldie's best home turns out to be Grandma's with the kids as godparents), and heroes help others, 'and those others don't have to be people.' Coping note: the blanket fort and the parents' memory of building one for the scared kids. Content considerations: a house fire (Dad safe, a girl rescued), a firefighter parent worried over, a wrecked party purse the kids repay. Topic note: no defensible topic; a want-a-pet and sibling-rivalry story fits none of the eight (the party mishap is a complication, not the center).

rows.synopsis: Lizzie needs help proving Shadow has what it takes to be a guide dog. Charles and Sammy work together to make the perfect puppy room.
rows.situation: feeling left out when your sibling's best friend takes over
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Shadow the guide-dog hopeful): Lizzie's blindfold experiment for her Helen Keller report, Charles's 'you and Sammy are always hanging out'. Learns: saying the left-out feeling out loud works ('It's what happens when you have a best friend, I guess'), and rules cannot always bend, but the right home beats the plan (Shadow becomes Wyatt's companion, no rule broken). Content considerations: blindness explored respectfully via the blindfold experiment, a child's allergy, a dog rehomed twice. Topic note: School & books on the report, the experiment and the project partnership.

rows.synopsis: While Charles sets out to find a home for an energetic Jack Russell terrier, Lizzie's ranch visit doesn't go according to plan.
rows.situation: pretending to love a friend's favorite thing
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Rascal the Jack Russell, the ranch weekend): Lizzie fakes her way through horseback riding until she confesses ('pretending... is just another way of saying that I wasn't being completely honest'). Learns: a best friend tells the truth even when it disappoints, and Maria owns her pressure ('I just wanted this weekend to be perfect'); Rascal finds his home where he can run, with a horse friend. Content considerations: a faked injury exposed, a dog rehomed. Topic note: no defensible topic; the friendship-honesty story has no controlled topic, and horseback riding is the setting.

rows.synopsis: Lizzie vows to help a German shepherd puppy join the search and rescue team. Charles gets carried away with a friendly debate over dogs and drones.
rows.situation: being scared, trapped, and learning what Dad does with his fear
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Scout the German shepherd, Safety Week): two kids locked in a shed, a drone crash, Scout sniffing out Charles's hat. Learns: being scared is part of a hard job, and a happy thought is a real tool ('when I'm scared, I think about dogs and my mom's Christmas chili... try thinking about something that makes you really happy'); Scout the training washout saves the day by not giving up. Content considerations: children trapped and calling for help, search-and-rescue peril described, a firefighter's dangerous job discussed. Topic note: no defensible topic; the school Safety Week demo is the frame, not the subject.

rows.synopsis: A needy pug puts Lizzie's internship at a doggy daycare to the test. Charles attempts to finish a school project while bingeing his favorite show.
rows.situation: blamed for an honest mistake at school
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Pugsley's daycare arc, service week): a missed sign-up (Sammy forgot Charles's name), Lizzie's internship under rules-first Ruth, the lost 'customer'. Learns: a loving reason plus honesty beats a rule ('I didn't volunteer because I like dogs. I volunteered because I love dogs'), and helping one dog well is the job done (the five-star review vindicates her). Coping note: 'Can I just say something really quick?' spoken up to the owner. Content considerations: a dog's separation anxiety handled warmly, an evaluation scare, composting explained. Topic note: School & books on service week and the joint project.

rows.synopsis: Charles agrees to foster an adorable but high-maintenance Yorkie pup. Lizzie gets paired with the school's judo champ for an assignment.
rows.situation: a high-needs responsibility all by yourself
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Princess the Yorkie, the ten-page decree list): Charles fosters alone while Lizzie works with judo champ JJ. Learns: ten pages of rules are just love in detail ('If I can do a hundred push-ups a day, I can handle a puppy'), being underestimated is fixed by showing not arguing ('everyone thinks I only care about judo. But I love school too'), and 'it's only scary once' (Remy's throw). Content considerations: a dog rehomed because of a world tour, a dad's pet allergy, missing a sibling (JJ's brother at college). Topic note: School & books on the ancient civilizations project; the judo thread stays a secondary mirror, not a tag.

rows.synopsis: The Petersons take in a sensitive boxer puppy that needs a one-on-one forever home. To get into a book club, Lizzie makes a promise she can't keep.
rows.situation: wanting into a group, and a friend's lie on your behalf
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Jack the boxer puppy, the Kit Smithers book club): Maria invents a friendship with the author, Lizzie confesses to the club ('I don't really know Kit Smithers... I don't have a pool, so I panicked'). Learns: the truth costs one awkward moment and buys real belonging, and losing a beloved pet deserves said-out-loud grief (Kit on Kaboodle: 'my heart hasn't been the same since he passed'). Content considerations: a dog's death remembered (offscreen, past), a lie exposed and owned, a sensitive puppy rehomed with the author. Topic note: School & books on the book club and author visit.

rows.synopsis: Charles, Lizzie, and Maria discover that Bandit, a playful shih tzu, needs surgery before they can find him the perfect companion.
rows.situation: a sick puppy, and the fear that you caused it
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Bandit the shih tzu, the heart valve condition): a raspy breath caught in time, the pancake-breakfast fundraiser. Learns: a heart condition is nobody's fault ('If it was your fault, I don't think Bandit would be asking you to hold him'), and a community can fund what one kid cannot ('Have a heart, help a heart'). Content considerations: a puppy's heart condition and surgery (resolved well, activity limits after), self-blame named and dispelled, a $4,000 cost discussed. Topic note: no defensible topic; the trebuchet school presentation is a running prop, not the subject.

rows.synopsis: Lizzie's Caring Paws Club comes up with an idea that's just what Charles needs to help a misunderstood rottweiler puppy.
rows.situation: the dog everyone has decided not to like
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Molly the rottweiler, Doggypalooza): the unfair reputation, Remy's fear fed by a comic-book villain, the photo-testimonial campaign. Learns: a breed is not a personality ('Rottweilers are like any other breed. Treat them with love and respect, and they will do the same'), and speaking up for a misunderstood friend flips it; a good leader uses everyone's ideas. Coping note: the campaign is advocacy, tagged standing up for yourself. Content considerations: breed prejudice named and corrected, a dog passed over for adoption, a one-eyed dog and an old dog shown with dignity. Topic note: no defensible topic; the Caring Paws Club campaign has no controlled topic.

rows.synopsis: Charles and Lizzie disagree on whether or not to separate two puppy siblings. Thankfully, they find the perfect compromise.
rows.situation: a friendship that broke, and two tiny lives in your hands
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Teeny and Tiny, the bottle-feeding week): around-the-clock feeds, a bus misunderstanding, the sit-down. Learns: 'I feel' sentences un-break a friendship ('This is a discussion, not an argument. Focus on listening'), and doing the parenting yourself shows you what your parents gave up. Content considerations: abandoned newborn puppies (mother unknown), a friendship rupture ('he called me boring'), a haircut mocked on the bus (a misunderstanding). Topic note: no defensible topic; a friendship-repair and tiny-puppies story fits none of the eight.

rows.synopsis: After Lizzie and Charles are each let down by friends, a stray mixed-breed pup teaches them valuable lessons about trust and friendship.
rows.situation: replaced on your best friend's calendar
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Lucky the border collie, the campout weekend): Maria cancels for Cara's French homework, new kid David joins Sammy, Lizzie alone with cookies. Learns: a new friend is not a replacement, and saying you felt left out beats sulking ('I'm sorry I made you feel like that. You weren't in the way at all'); a lost dog with a thorn finds her way home. Content considerations: a canceled sleepover, a dog's sore paw treated gently, a move mentioned in passing. Topic note: no defensible topic; the camping and trivia frame carries no controlled topic.

rows.synopsis: The kids stumble on a dog and her puppies at the bookstore and try to find homes for them—while keeping it a secret from their parents.
rows.situation: a shy kid who only feels safe with a dog
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Buddy, the box outside Cozy Nook Books, the Book Worms revival): shy Parker who speaks up only when Buddy is near, the staged one-puppy-first plan ('giving the truth some breathing room'), the come-clean. Learns: comfort is a need, not a weakness ('Buddy is what Parker needed to feel calm and at ease around the other kids'), and truth stretched thin is still not the whole truth; Buddy the food-hider is safe and loved. Content considerations: puppies abandoned in a box, a shy child, food-hiding from early scarcity explained. Topic note: School & books on the reading-program revival.

rows.synopsis: When Lizzie trains an energetic sheltie for a competition, it's unclear who wants to win more: her or the dog.
rows.situation: freezing up in the game, and a coach who will not let winning be the point
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Gizmo the sheltie, the agility assessment): Charles's missed baskets ('I freeze up every time someone passes me the ball'), Dad the former captain coaching, Lizzie reading Gizmo's plopped-down refusals. Learns: the dog decides what fun is ('if Gizmo's not having fun anymore, then there's no point'), and a kid decides to play again after every miss; Gizmo's home is the one with a basketball. Content considerations: none significant; competitive pressure named and relaxed, a dog retired from training. Topic note: Sports & games on the basketball and agility-competition thread.

rows.synopsis: Charles meets a retirement home resident whose lifestyle makes her the perfect companion for a scrappy West Highland terrier.
rows.situation: a disagreement you decide to hear out instead of win
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Snowball the Westie, the class pet Eddie, the grand buddies program): the class-pet welfare debate, Lizzie and Maria each switching sides, the class-plant compromise. Learns: an argument can change your mind and keep your friend ('anytime we disagree on something... we will always hear each other out'), and an animal's needs outrank the fun (Ulysses S. Plant takes over). Content considerations: the class-pet welfare debate handled with sourced arguments on both sides, retirement-home residents shown warmly and usefully (Rose and Snowball). Topic note: School & books on the class pet program and debate team.

rows.synopsis: While visiting cousins Becky and Steph, Charles and Lizzie find a lost border collie. Returning the pup helps Steph appreciate her new home.
rows.situation: a cousin who came home from the move a different person
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Flash the border collie, the Andover visit): Steph in 'Steph mode' since the Manhattan move, the frisbee clue, the reunion with Chloe the pizza-shop dog. Learns: a move can shrink a person until someone plays their game with them ('sorry if I was acting weird. I was so stressed'), and city kids and country kids can share a mystery. Content considerations: a recent move and homesickness, a lost dog (safe return), a ladder fall in backstory. Topic note: no defensible topic; the farm-stand food cameos are scenery, not the subject.

rows.synopsis: Charles and Lizzie rally their friends to help look for a missing dachshund. The kids may finally be ready for a dog of their own.
rows.situation: the first failure, and a whole town of helpers
rows.notes: script-verified (Gestdown, identity-checked: Ziggy the dachshund, Unity Quest, Buddy's return): a returned adoption that shakes Lizzie ('I just feel so bad for placing Buddy with the wrong family'), the walkie-talkie network, the Unity Quest mirror. Learns: failure happens to people who try ('people who say "Failure is not an option" are totally unrealistic'), unity wins the real quest ('we must unite, or else we fall'), and the dog you failed is the dog you keep (the look between the parents says yes). Coping note: 'Can we help? Yeah. We can all work together.' Content considerations: a failed adoption handled with care (the other family heartbroken), a lost dog (safe return). Topic note: Sports & games on the Unity Quest game that frames and teaches the cooperation lesson.
